title: Interactive: Tracking negotiating texts at the COP31 climate summit - Carbon Brief
gist: Carbon Brief launches a real-time tracker of negotiating texts at COP31 in Antalya, where nearly 200 nations, excluding the US, negotiate 104 substantive agenda items under a joint Turkey-Australia leadership arrangement. Key items include a possible cover text acknowledging 1.5C overshoot and a Turkish target for electricity to supply 35% of final energy by 2035, the global goal on adaptation, the mitigation work programme, a new just transition mechanism, and African-group pushes on climate-related trade tariffs and adaptation finance.

insights.claim: At COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, diplomats from nearly 200 nations, not including the US, will try to reach consensus on more than 100 separate agreements over the two-week summit.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: US absence reduces the weight of COP outcomes for US-exposed climate policy.

insights.claim: Turkey holds the COP31 presidency and hosts the summit while Australia jointly runs it as 'president of negotiations', and the pair plan an overarching political 'cover text' summarising outcomes and off-agenda issues.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The cover text is where headline political signals, rather than legal commitments, will appear.

insights.claim: Ahead of the opening, Carbon Brief's tracker counts 104 substantive items on the COP31 agenda excluding procedural matters, and the summit is not seen as a banner year because it falls halfway between two global stocktakes.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Expect incremental rather than market-moving outcomes from COP31.
insights.locator: Ahead of the opening of the summit

insights.claim: The COP31 cover text could recognise that warming is set to overshoot the 1.5C limit and include the Turkish presidency's target for 35% of global final energy to come from electricity by 2035.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: An electrification target would be a supportive signal for grid, power-equipment and EV supply chains.

insights.claim: Major COP31 topics include finalising the global goal on adaptation, deciding whether to continue the contested mitigation work programme, and agreeing details of a new just transition mechanism known as the Belém-Antalya mechanism (BAM).
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Adaptation and just-transition finance are the likely areas of incremental funding flows.

insights.claim: COP30 added two items to future agendas: developed countries' provision of climate finance under Paris Agreement Article 9.1 and aligning global finance flows with the treaty under Article 2.1c.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Article 2.1c discussions bear on how financial institutions align portfolios with climate goals.

insights.claim: The African group filed a request to add climate-related trade tariffs to the COP31 agenda, beyond the annual Bonn dialogues agreed at COP30, and also seeks items on tripling adaptation finance and funding the Green Climate Fund.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Carbon border tariffs such as EU-style measures face growing multilateral pushback.

insights.claim: Carbon Brief's tracker colour-codes agenda items from red (no text) to orange (informal text), yellow (draft legal text with brackets and options), green (agreed) and grey (postponed under rule 16), and counts outstanding brackets and options as a gauge of disagreement.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Bracket counts offer a real-time signal of which COP outcomes are likely to land.

insights.claim: Final gavelling of draft decisions at the closing plenary is usually a formality, but at COP29 the president failed to adopt a deal on the 2023 global stocktake that had called for transitioning away from fossil fuels.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Fossil-fuel transition language remains fragile and can collapse at the last step.
